highlight.title: Go live from your browser — no OBS needed
highlight.text: Press Go Live, allow your camera and microphone, and you're live, with your own channel and chat. There's nothing to install and no follower or subscriber minimum. It works on a Chromebook, a laptop or a phone.
points: No OBS, plug-ins or capture card: WebRTC in the browser, with under a second of delay
No follower, subscriber or past-stream requirement
Share your screen, a window or a tab, with your camera over it
When you want scenes, use OBS or any RTMP or WHIP encoder

faq: Can I stream without OBS?
Yes. Go live from your browser on OpenVibe.Live: press Go Live, allow your camera and microphone, and you are live. There is nothing to install.
Do I need followers or subscribers to go live?
No. Every OpenVibe account can go live from the first minute, with no follower, subscriber or past-stream requirement.
Can I stream from a Chromebook or a phone?
Yes. The broadcaster runs in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, on ChromeOS, Android and iOS as well as Windows, macOS and Linux.
Can I restream to Twitch, YouTube and Kick at the same time?
Yes. One broadcast can go to Twitch, YouTube, Kick and any RTMP, RTMPS or SRT server at once.
Can I use OBS if I want to?
Yes. OBS and any RTMP encoder work, and so do WHIP encoders (OBS 30 and later, ffmpeg, GStreamer).

viz.name: Rover-1
viz.caption: Design preview of the robot panel
viz.label: Design preview: a robot control panel with live video, a drive pad, buttons, battery level and a stop button

vision.stepsLead: No port forwarding, no stream keys, no config files.
steps: Name it and pick what it is: a rover, an arm, a camera, a phone on wheels or your own design.
Paste one command on the robot, flash a ready-made card, or scan a QR code. It gets its own key, which you can revoke any time.
Live video and controls in any browser, phone included, with a stop button that always works.

choices.title: Buy one or bring your own
choices.lead: Start with hardware that is known to work, or use what you already have.

items.title: Get a robot
items.text: Curated kits with parts lists, tested settings and build guides, and ready-made bots that arrive paired to your account. The first one on OpenVibe.Bot is the Adeept 4WD Smart Car for Raspberry Pi.

items.title: Bring your own
items.text: Anything with motors, a camera or sensors. Install the OpenVibe device agent on the robot, or, for robots with their own firmware like Cozmo, on a computer next to it, and your robot shows up in the panel.

vision.featuresLead: A control panel for anything you build, whether or not anyone is watching.
features: Drive pad, keyboard, touch joystick and gamepad; buttons, sliders, servos and camera pan-tilt, laid out from your robot's profile.
Video and commands over WebRTC, so driving feels direct. Works behind ordinary home and mobile networks.
Invite friends as operators, or open a public queue with timed turns, cooldowns and per-role limits.
The robot stops itself when commands stop. An emergency stop, speed and range limits and time windows, all logged.
Schedules, triggers and webhooks, plus an API and SDKs for your own apps.
Let your OpenVibe.Actor agent patrol, check on or perform with your robot, with your approval.
vision.connectTitle: Stream it, record it, connect it
vision.connectLead: Optional, one toggle each. Your robot does not need an audience to be useful.
connect: Put the robot's camera on your channel; viewers can drive it from chat or the panel.
Low-latency ingest and restreaming to other platforms from the same camera.
Keep every run as a video and cut clips from it.
vision.building: OpenVibe.Bot is being built now, starting with our own robots; stream-controlled robots already run on OpenVibe.Live.

faq: Do I need to open ports on my router?
No. The robot connects out to OpenVibe, and video and controls travel over WebRTC, so it works behind ordinary home and mobile networks.
Is it only for streaming?
No. Streaming is optional. Bot is a control panel for your robot first: drive it, check on it, share it and automate it.
Which robot comes first?

The Adeept 4WD Smart Car Kit for Raspberry Pi: four motors, a pan-tilt camera, distance and line sensors, lights and a buzzer. OpenVibe's device agent drives it directly, so its own open control port never has to be exposed.
Does it work with Cozmo?

Yes, built in. Cozmo makes its own Wi-Fi and runs closed firmware, so the OpenVibe agent runs on a computer next to it (a Raspberry Pi or a laptop) that joins Cozmo's Wi-Fi and stays online through another connection. You get driving, the head and lift, its camera, its face display, its voice, lights and cubes, and it stops at edges on its own. No phone app needed.
What hardware works?
A Raspberry Pi or another Linux board, an ESP32, a ROS 2 robot, an Android phone, or an ONVIF or RTSP camera. The curated kits list exactly what to buy.
How does it keep the robot safe?
The device stops its motors by itself when commands or the connection stop. There is an emergency stop in the panel, limits on speed, range and time, and every command is logged.
What will it cost?
Controlling your own robot will not cost anything. Limits and any paid extras will be published before launch.

faq: Is this like OpenRouter?
Yes, for agents: one API and one bill for many agent systems, with live prices and rankings. Actor routes whole tasks rather than single model calls, and it checks the results before you get them.
Which agent systems does it use?
OpenVibe's own runtime, hosted agent platforms from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, coding agents, and open-source agents on OpenVibe's hardware. Each is an adapter, so new ones join quickly.
How does it choose?
For each kind of task it compares price, speed, success rate and current health across agent systems, then applies your mode and budget. Every choice is recorded and explained.
Can I keep my data on OpenVibe?
Yes. Private mode uses only OpenVibe's own runtime and open models on its own hardware.
Can it act without asking?
Only as far as you allow. Anything with consequences, like publishing, spending or moving a robot, waits for your approval, and every action is logged.
What will it cost?
You will be able to start without paying, within limits published before launch; bigger tasks and stronger agents will be paid, with the cost shown per task.

sites.name: OpenVibe.Events
sites.tagline: Events, queues and webhooks you can build on.
sites.description: OpenVibe.Events is the network's event system: durable events, topics and subscriptions, signed webhooks with retries, dead-letter queues and replay, pull consumers with checkpoints, and realtime delivery to browsers with cursor resume. Every OpenVibe product already publishes through it. This domain becomes its home, with queues, streams, project namespaces and developer tools.
pillars: Fan out to subscribers with signed, retried deliveries.
Competing consumers with leases, and ordered history with cursors.
Server-sent events to browsers, resuming where they left off.
Nothing is lost quietly: replay it, or inspect what failed.
